projects.title: Villiger Arrow
projects.description: A Villiger Arrow sourced from the local Velobörse; painted with the same technique as seen on [Red Road](https://seiden-design-labs.com/project?id=red-road). Almost all parts aside from the frame and suspension fork were replaced with newer components, the 3x7 drivetrain was swapped for a single speed setup.

projects.title: BrechSchnell
projects.description:
A gravel bicycle built primarily with components sourced from aliexpress; notable components are the 11-speed LTWOO drivetrain and the TRP HYRD brake calipers. 

The inspiration for the paintwork stemmed from the fact that the frame vendor had used multiple A4 sheets of chinese stamps to cover the postage fee. 

The Green-Gold colors reference the Chinese Postal Service (China Post), the beige and red colors represent packaging and shipping labels. The stamps were integrated into the paintwork and continue to travel together with the frame.

projects.title: Miami Cruiser
projects.description:
A beach cruiser painted in a miami-style color scheme; the paint effect was achieved using a crumpled plastic bag to create the marbled texture.

The rim of the rear wheel is decorated with the RGPB logo and hand-laced.

projects.title: Red Road
projects.description:
A Triban RC 120 (Decathlon) painted in red; the paint effect was achieved using a plastic bag to create a silver marbled texture over a red base, which was then covered with red candy paint and clear coat.

The bicycle was sold to a friend in Switzerland in 2026.

projects.title: AEK II Mini
projects.materials: Wood, Metal, ALPS switches (white), PBT (Keycaps), ABS (Spacebar)
projects.description:
A keyboard with a 60% layout, built using components harvested from a broken [Apple Extended Keyboard II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_keyboards#Macintosh_Keyboard_(M0110)), this keyboard is equipped with white ALPS switches. 

The custom backplate for this keyboard was made on request by a fellow keyboard enthusiast in Sweden. The keyboard matrix is hand-wired with an Atmega32u4 controller. Hydrogen peroxide was used to reverse the yellowing on the ABS spacebar.

The keyboard was given to a friend in Switzerland in 2016.

Inspired by the [M0110](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_keyboards#Macintosh_Keyboard_(M0110)) from Apple and the [Ducky Mini (2014)](https://ducky.global/products/year-of-the-horse-2014) from Ducky.

projects.title: PoorPad
projects.materials: Acrylic, Printed Circuit Board (Copper, FR4), Atmega32u4, Diodes, Cherry/Gateron Switches
projects.description:
A numpad designed to be inexpensive and fully programmable. Designed for serial production of 25 units. 

The acrylic case and PCB layout are custom-made for the PoorPad project.

projects.title: Tada68 Numpad
projects.materials: ABS, Gateron Clear Switches, Atmega32u4, Diodes, Wire
projects.description:
This number pad was designed to address the lack of a number pad on the Tada68, a 65%-layout keyboard. The case was designed to match the geometry of the body of the Tada68, the numpad features gateron clear switches with an actuation force of 35g. The internal electronics are hand-wired with an Atmega32u4 controller. Spray paint was used to smoothen the 3D-printed surface.

This numpad is currently on display in my living room.

projects.title: SpeedPad
projects.materials: ABS, Gateron Red Switches, Atmega32u4 Breakout Board, Diodes, Cable, Glue
projects.description:
Inspired by racecar-style beds and designed as a practical joke, this state of the art input device takes the form of a standalone number pad. The keyboard matrix has been hand-wired with an Atmega32u4 breakout board, allowing for full programmability of the device.
A red LED was added to provide for undercarriage lighting and to increase the top speed, at the cost of increased heat.

The SpeedPad was sold to a customer in the USA in 2016.

projects.title: WoodBoard
projects.materials: Wood, PCB ([GON's Keyboard Works](https://geon.works/)), Gateron Red Switches
projects.description:
A backplate-less keyboard featuring a laser-cut wooden case with PCB-mount switches. The assembly is a sandwich-style case with two glued layers attached to the bottom layer with fine wood screws. The keycaps were taken from a Cherry G80-1800.

This keyboard was fabricated for and subsequently given to a friend in Switzerland.

projects.title: PrintKeeb
projects.description: A keyboard case designed to print as two split halves in order to accomodate the printbed sizes of most 3D-printers. After a few round of protoyping, the project was abandoned for a lack of technical viability relative to pre-fabricated alternatives.

projects.title: ReLa
projects.description:
This project arose from a discarded desk lamp and a need for direct lighting over my workspace. The diffuser and electronical housing and controls are 3D-printed, the articulating arm and lampshade were donated by the discarded desk lamp. The light can be turned on/off and dimmed via the three-button interface, inside the housing is a simple dimmer circuit sourced from AliExpress and a cable leading to a generic 12v power supply. The light inside the lamp is provided by a set of LED strips behind the diffuser.

The lamp was discarded at a later time when the aforementioned workspace ceased to exist.

projects.title: RoLa
projects.description: This lamp was designed to address a lack of interior lighting in my living room. The body is 3d printed with an LED strip and a potentiometer acting as a dimmer and is powered by a generic 12v power supply. The lamp is dimmed by rotating the lampshade.
